sections.guidance: GitHub says users with an inactive session from that period may still be signed out and need only sign in again. For the Copilot incident it recommended choosing another model or selecting 'Fusion'.

items.headline: Google reports first fully automated AI exploitation pipeline, with French sites targeted
items.summary: Google's GTIG says an exposed staging server revealed 'exploit_agent', an AI pipeline that diffed patches, wrote and ran exploits without human input. Victim data pointed to French media, entertainment and education sites. Operator unnamed; Russian-language comments only.
items.label: VENDOR-ACKNOWLEDGED
items.labelBasis: Google's own threat report; no victim or French authority confirmation found.
items.firstReported: 16 Nov 2026, Google Cloud GTIG blog (AI Threat Tracker); CyberScoop same day

sections.happened: On 16 November 2026 Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant published a quarterly AI Threat Tracker. It says that, for the first time, GTIG identified actors using LLM frameworks to automate vulnerability discovery and exploitation without a human in the loop. GTIG found an exposed staging server hosting 'exploit_agent'. Victim telemetry suggested interest in French websites in media, entertainment and education. Coverage then described it as the first autonomous AI cyberattack; the 'first' claim is Google's.
sections.technical: exploit_agent chains multiple agents with frontier and local LLMs and runs continuous differential analysis of popular web application software: it compares pre- and post-patch code, infers flaws, drafts exploits and executes them. One example analysed the Spectra (Ultimate Addons for Gutenberg) WordPress plugin v2.19.25. The server also held scripts for reconnaissance, brute-forcing, webshell installation and removal of rival webshells. Russian-language comments sit in a configuration file for LLM API keys. No CVEs, IOCs or ATT&CK IDs were published for this operation.
sections.guidance: Google says Google SecOps deployed rulepacks to detect the ARTEX tool, and Mandiant Consulting released a hardening guide and architectural defence framework against LLM-enabled offensive tooling.
sections.differing: Google calls the operators 'Russian-speaking' based on code comments; it names no group or state. Secondary outlets (Politico-sourced reports) repeat this; some aggregators go further, calling it a 'Russian APT', which Google's report does not support.
sections.unknown: Victim names, number of compromised sites, success rate, the targeted software versions and operator identity are unpublished. French authorities have not commented in the sources read.

sources.title: Google Cloud GTIG: AI Threat Tracker, Agentic Threat Activity Crosses a Significant Threshold
CyberScoop: Google says Russian-speaking hackers ran the first fully automated AI cyberattack

items.headline: Study: cloud keys planted in Docker Hub images used within seconds
items.summary: Stony Brook researchers planted 300 honeypot images on eight registries; planted AWS keys drew API calls within 7.86 seconds, and 100 Docker Hub keys were used within 15 minutes.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Peer-reviewed ACM CCS 2026 paper reported by BleepingComputer and iThome; paper not read directly. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: 17 Nov 2026, 21:27 UK time; BleepingComputer (16:27 ET)

sections.happened: Stony Brook researchers Billy Tsouvalas and Nick Nikiforakis published 300 honeypot images on eight public registries over four months, presented at ACM CCS 2026. Images were pulled over 75,000 times; planted AWS keys drew over 140,000 API calls.
sections.technical: Scanners appear to extract keys by static analysis of image layers or registry APIs, without running containers. Planted AWS keys were used within 7.86 seconds (iThome); OpenAI and Anthropic test keys were also used. No CVE is involved.
sections.guidance: Researchers recommend Docker Hub scan images for secrets before publication, warn publishers, and limit access to its public feed of new images. iThome advises revoking or rotating exposed keys, not only deleting images.
sections.differing: Windowsforum notes the study is a controlled experiment and cannot say how many real public images contain secrets.
sections.unknown: Paper not read directly. Whether Docker has responded is not reported. Figures come from press coverage of the researchers' findings.

items.headline: Cisco Expressway CVE-2026-76466 exploited after public PoC, F6 reports
items.summary: F6 says attackers used a public proof-of-concept for critical Cisco Expressway flaw CVE-2026-76466 (CVSS 9.8) to gain root on clustered devices at a Russian organisation. Cisco's advisory, unrevised, still says it knows of no malicious use.
items.label: VENDOR-ACKNOWLEDGED
items.labelBasis: Flaw confirmed by Cisco; exploitation reported only by F6 via SecurityWeek.
items.firstReported: SecurityWeek, November 2026 (time not stated in page)

sections.happened: Cisco disclosed CVE-2026-76466 in Expressway on 21 October 2026. Security firm F6 reports attackers exploited it against an unnamed Russian organisation soon after a PoC appeared on GitHub. They breached two internet-exposed Expressway X15.5.3 devices, then moved to two internal cluster nodes. F6 did not name the victim or attribute the attack to a known actor.
sections.technical: Unauthenticated remote root command execution (CVSS 9.8, CWE-798) in the Expressway database service, affecting clustered Expressway Core and Edge. Cause: persistent cookies and unvalidated client certificates when clustering TLS Verify Mode is enabled; attacker invokes RPC commands. After root, attackers used custom Python scripts for scanning, SMB, SQL Server, WinRM and GitLab searches, apparently AI-assisted per code comments. Detection: Erlang system log; F6 published IPs and file paths.
sections.guidance: Cisco: Expressway X15.5.20 fixes the flaw; no workarounds; X14 and earlier must move to a fixed release. F6 suggests, if patching is not possible, blocking TCP 4371–4372 except from trusted cluster node IPs.
sections.differing: Cisco's advisory, unrevised per SecurityWeek, says it is unaware of malicious use; F6 reports in-the-wild exploitation. F6's report is the only account.
sections.unknown: Victim identity, attacker, number of affected devices, and whether Cisco will confirm exploitation are unknown; SecurityWeek awaited Cisco comment.

sources.title: Cisco Security Advisory: Cisco Expressway Series Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

items.headline: VMware vCenter zero-day CVE-2026-123890 exploited by suspected China-nexus Armory Castle since September
items.summary: Broadcom patched a critical vCenter authentication bypass (CVE-2026-123890, CVSS 9.8) on 19 November. Google Mandiant says suspected Chinese group Armory Castle exploited it from early September, after a BeyondTrust zero-day. Broadcom's advisory does not mention exploitation.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Broadcom advisory plus Mandiant analysis, reported consistently by multiple outlets and Rapid7. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: 19 Nov 2026 (evening UK), BleepingComputer; Broadcom advisory VMSA-2026-0009 published 19 Nov

sections.happened: Broadcom published VMSA-2026-0009 on 19 November 2026, fixing five flaws, including CVE-2026-123890, a CVSS 9.8 authentication bypass in the vCenter VMware Directory Service. Google's Mandiant, which reported the bug, says suspected China-nexus group Armory Castle (formerly UNC5221) exploited it in early September, over two months before the patch, inside networks already breached via a BeyondTrust Remote Support zero-day (CVE-2026-102764). Mandiant investigated multiple incidents; victims are not named.
sections.technical: Mandiant describes an unauthenticated SRP-6a session key disclosure over DCE/RPC (port 2012) yielding an administrator@vsphere.local session. Tool BONESAW (Go) exfiltrates the LMDB (data.mdb), SAML signing material and creates an SSO admin; SAWSNAKE forges Golden SAML tokens. Other tooling: SLIMSAVAGE, CAGEMATCH, BEARBONES, LAZYBONES (Slack C2), BARECLAW. Attackers then enabled SSH via VAMI and accessed ESXi. Fixed: 9.1.1.0200, 9.0.2.0200, 8.0 U3m, VCF 5.2.5. 7.0 has no public patch.
sections.guidance: Broadcom classes the update as an emergency change and lists no workaround, noting its FAQ says network restrictions and firewall controls may reduce exposure. Mandiant's CTO Charles Carmakal advises both patching and examining systems for evidence of compromise. vCenter 7.0 extended-support customers are directed to Broadcom Support.
sections.differing: Broadcom's advisory does not mention in-the-wild exploitation; exploitation and attribution come from Mandiant/Google, which calls the actor 'suspected' China-nexus. Build timestamp suggesting prior knowledge is noted as modifiable.
sections.unknown: Victim count, sectors and data stolen are undisclosed. Whether the 7.0 branch will be patched is unclear. Attribution is not confirmed by any government.

items.headline: Researcher publishes unpatched Windows 'FastUnlock' lock-screen bypass using Narrator
items.summary: Researcher Chaotic Eclipse (MSNightmare) published FastUnlock, an unpatched Windows 11 lock-screen bypass abusing Narrator to run code as the limited WsiAccount. It needs physical access. ThreatLocker reproduced it; no Microsoft fix or in-the-wild use reported.
items.label: VENDOR-ACKNOWLEDGED
items.labelBasis: Reproduced by ThreatLocker per The Hacker News; Microsoft has not responded.
items.firstReported: 19 Nov 2026, GitHub repository MSNightmare/FastUnlock (reported by Security Affairs, 19 Nov)

sections.happened: On 19 November 2026 the researcher known as Chaotic Eclipse, MSNightmare or Nightmare-Eclipse (who has identified himself as Abdelhamid Naceri) published FastUnlock on GitHub with a video. It is a Narrator-based Windows lock-screen bypass. He claims it breached a BitLocker-encrypted Windows 11 26H2 machine with November updates in five minutes. The Hacker News says ThreatLocker tested it the same day and it worked. No Microsoft fix exists and no real-world attack is reported.
sections.technical: Attack needs physical access and an account tied to a Microsoft account. From the 'I forgot my PIN' recovery screen, enabling Narrator focuses a hidden window; keyboard navigation reaches Narrator settings, then File Explorer via Bluetooth and Devices or AutoPlay. Code runs as the non-administrator WsiAccount. Researcher says Narrator's redesigned interface is allowed to run in the lock-screen context. It does not break BitLocker: with TPM-only unlock the drive is already decrypted. No CVE or CVSS published; Windows 10 untested.
sections.guidance: The Hacker News, citing Microsoft's countermeasures guidance, lists a BitLocker startup PIN and shutting down or hibernating devices that leave the user's control. No Microsoft advisory or patch exists yet.
sections.differing: The researcher says it 'bypasses BitLocker'; ThreatLocker-based reporting says it does not break encryption, since the TPM has already unlocked the drive. The latter is better supported technically.
sections.unknown: Affected Windows versions, whether Microsoft has a fix planned, whether the researcher notified Microsoft, and whether full USB code execution was demonstrated (the researcher did not show it).

sources.title: FastUnlock - GitHub repository (researcher, primary)

sections.technical: Buchanan and co-conspirators sent smishing texts impersonating employers and IT suppliers, harvested credentials via a phishing kit relayed to a Telegram channel, then used SIM swaps to take over victims' crypto accounts. Activity ran September 2021 to April 2023.
sections.guidance: Malwarebytes advises asking the mobile carrier for an account PIN, port-out lock or number-transfer protection, and preferring authenticator apps, passkeys or security keys over SMS codes.
sections.differing: Malwarebytes calls Buchanan British; Bitcoin Magazine and Decrypt say Scottish. Group-IB says Scattered Spider is fragmented, so the sentence does not mean the group has ended.
sections.unknown: Restitution amount is unsettled. Reported loss ranges from $8 million to $11.6 million. Which cryptocurrencies were taken was not disclosed.

sections.happened: Sean Cairncross, the US national cyber director, was fired on Thursday 19 November. A White House official told The Hill that President Trump backed the decision. Kirsten Davies, the Defense Department chief information officer, becomes acting director. Axios reported it first. CBS sources said chief of staff Stephen Miller had long wanted him out. Outlets tie the timing to recent outages affecting travel, communications, banking and an internal National Security Agency system.
sections.differing: AFP's source linked the dismissal to the outages. The White House official quoted by The Hill instead said Trump thought Cairncross lacked the proper cyber credentials. CBS sources cite Miller's view of his expertise. No official has attributed the outages to him.
sections.unknown: Whether the outages caused the dismissal, the outages' causes, and whether Davies will be formally nominated are not stated.

items.headline: House panel releases data on 879,000 AI chips licensed for China; California AG subpoenas Nvidia
items.summary: House Foreign Affairs Committee documents show US approved 879,000 of 3.4 million requested Nvidia/AMD AI chips for China. California's attorney general separately subpoenaed Nvidia over possible chip or data diversion following ex-CEO Jensen Huang's resignation.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Committee documents, California AG press release and company statements reported by CNBC and The Register.
items.firstReported: 19 Nov 2026 (evening UK), CNBC and California AG press release

sections.happened: On 19 November the House Foreign Affairs Committee voted to release export-licence data. It says companies requested 3.4 million AI chips for China (December to May) and the Bureau of Industry and Security approved 879,000, including for Alibaba and Tencent, both on the Pentagon's Chinese military companies list. Requests for 610,000 (Alibaba) and 508,000 (ByteDance) chips were refused. Separately, California Attorney General Rob Bonta served an investigative subpoena on Nvidia asking whether chips or confidential information reached China and whether investors were misled. This follows Jensen Huang's resignation over an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.
sections.guidance: Nvidia said it followed Commerce rules in force at the time and has stopped shipping H200s to China. Nvidia and AMD say they comply with US export law. BIS said licences carried strict conditions and limited volumes.
sections.differing: Chairman Mast says approvals ran against policy intent and some applications involved diversion fronts. Nvidia, AMD and BIS say processes were lawful. Bernstein's Stacy Rasgon calls 879,000 'not that many'; Beijing's import limits kept shipments small.
sections.unknown: Subpoena scope, deadline and any California legal claim are unstated. How many approved chips shipped is unreported. Megaspeed's links rest on New York Times reporting.

sections.happened: Taiwan flagged nearly 2,700 social media accounts to Meta, about 2,400 on Threads, which officials say form a Chinese information campaign targeting the 28 November local elections. Meta said it removed the flagged accounts, many already disabled, and that none posted election content.

items.headline: Coalition of the Willing urges Russia to accept winter energy ceasefire; Kushner cites Article 5-based guarantees
items.summary: After a Berlin summit on 19 November, Germany, France, the UK and Ukraine asked Russia for a winter energy ceasefire and a Black Sea food-export truce. Kushner said Russia accepts Article 5-based guarantees; Zelensky questioned the shared meaning. Putin ruled out truces.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Joint statement reported by Ukrinform and Kyiv Independent; Kushner and Zelensky quoted by Meduza. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: 19 Nov 2026, 23:05 UK time (Kyiv Independent; time as displayed on page)

sections.happened: A Coalition of the Willing summit in Berlin on 19 November, with over 40 partners and US envoys Witkoff and Kushner, produced a joint statement from Germany, France, the UK and Ukraine. It called on Russia to agree an energy ceasefire for the winter and a Black Sea ceasefire for food exports. It restated EUR 90bn EU loan support, air defence priorities, sanctions pressure and security guarantees including a European-led Multinational Force Ukraine.
sections.guidance: The leaders' statement says guarantees must be legally binding, defensive and closely coordinated with the US. It also says frozen Russian assets stay immobilised until Russia ends the war and compensates Ukraine.
sections.differing: Kushner said Russia is comfortable with guarantees based on Article 5. Zelensky doubted both sides mean the same thing, saying it implies partner forces on Ukrainian soil. Putin said the Crimean Bridge strike ended any talk of energy or Black Sea truces, and he opposes foreign troops (Kyiv Independent, Meduza).
sections.unknown: Whether Russia will accept any truce, what the US means by Article 5-based guarantees, and when the multilateral talks with European participation will take place.
